newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD sees 1997 German budget deficit 3.4 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: SPD sees 1997 German budget deficit 3.4 pct of GDP.

text.p: Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) forecast on Thursday that Germany's 1997 budget deficit would be 3.4 percent of economic output, missing the target for participating in the planned single European currency.
SPD budget spokesman Karl Diller told journalists Germany would not meet the Maastricht target of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1998 or 1999 either.
The reason is that government outlays for unemployment benefits would be 10 billion marks above budgeted levels, while tax revenues would be 20 billion marks lower, Diller said.

The convergence reported presented by the German government to the European Commission, showing that Germany would hit the target, is based on outdated data, Diller said, adding that Germany's deficit would be much higher than Finance Minister Theo Waigel has forecast.
Diller said the SPD would block any effort by Waigel to make early use of credits scheduled for 1998.
